summary: Klamath County lookout at Bly: 1934 warehouse-roof platform, then a 20-ft tower with a 7x7 cab (1958). Tower dismantled 2007; cab now in a community park. No staff named.

facts.design: 20-foot wooden tower with a 7x7 flat-roof cab and catwalk (1958); the first lookout was a 1934 platform on a warehouse roof
facts.status_note: Tower superstructure destroyed in 2007; the cab was moved to the community park in Bly.

staffing.status: emergency use only; no lookout staff named in the sources

access.note: The cab is in Bly's community park, less than a mile from the ranger station (2022 travel blog). No source says whether visitors may go inside the cab.

events.note: First lookout: a platform on the roof of a warehouse at the Klamath Forest Protective Association station
20-foot wooden tower with a 7x7 flat-roof cab, built at the Forest Service ranger station compound. The register's Built field says 1950; FFLOS says mid-1950s
Lookout decommissioned and scheduled to move to a local park as an interpretive center; the move was delayed a year for lack of a way to move the building
Tower dismantled and its superstructure destroyed (Weebly and blog say 2007; the 2006 decommissioning is in Weebly)
Cab moved to the community park in Bly

corrections.proposed: 1958 built (20-foot tower); 1934 first platform on the warehouse roof
corrections.why: The register's own description says the 20-foot tower was constructed in 1958. Weebly gives 1958 and the 2022 blog says the tower was constructed in 1958. FFLOS says mid-1950s. Only the register's Built field gives 1950.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's Built field says 1950; its description says 1958. Weebly gives 1958; FFLOS says the tower went up in the mid-1950s. The record's 1950 is contradicted by the register's own description, so 1958 is proposed.
Weebly says the lookout was decommissioned in 2006 and dismantled in 2007. The travel blog and firelookout.com date the dismantling to 2007.
The register gives 4,365 ft (1,330 m). FFLOS and firelookout.com give 4,400 ft. The record's 1330.5 m follows the register.

notes_for_editor: The 1934 platform and the 2007 move of the cab are well supported. The tower date is disputed: 1950 in the register's Built field, 1958 in its own description and in Weebly, mid-1950s in FFLOS. No source names a lookout who staffed it. The park name The Perch and the June 2022 visit come from a single personal travel blog. The brief's source list points to a sister record, us-or-bly-ranger-at-bly-city-park, which I did not read.
